results.content: NEW YORK, July 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index® decreased by 1.4 points to 90.8 (1985=100) in July, down from an upwardly revised 92.2 in June. The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—fell by 3.6 points to 114.9, its third consecutive monthly decline. The Expectations Index—based on consumers' short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions—remained unchanged at 74.7. results.content:
“Consumer confidence moderated slightly in July, continuing a general downward sloping trajectory since late 2021,” Dana M. Peterson, chief economist at The Conference Board, said in a release. “The Present Situation Index was less positive for a third consecutive month while the Expectations Index remained in negative territory.”

The board’s Present Situation Index — measuring consumers’ current assessment of business and labor market conditions — fell by 3.6 points to 114.9 in July.
